findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an existing client reruns a design folder created before upgrading Forge.
The fix updates the managed renderer, but src/forge/templates/story.md:17-18 instructs workers to copy and commit a separate support.js beside the screens. Sync ships only .forge/design/support.js (src/forge/story.py:91), so an already-copied renderer retains the old race and can still save about:blank at either width. The earlier-adopted test copies the new renderer after sync (tests/test_renderer_waits_for_page.py:54-55), so it does not cover this path.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - running Forge's configured full test suite on Windows.
The test passes an extensionless JavaScript file with a Unix shebang as CHROME_BIN, and the renderer spawns that path directly (src/forge/templates/design/support.js:46). Windows cannot execute that file as a program, so both test cases fail in the pytest suite configured by forge.toml:6. The Windows workflow selects only tests marked platform (.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:140), but this test has no such mark, so that workflow will not catch the failure. See the [Windows process-creation contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw).
findings.title: Keep the renderer regression test executable on Windows

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - the readiness check accepts the initial blank document.
The fake browser never evaluates the supplied readiness expression: it returns its own loaded flag for any expression other than the measurement. Replacing the new condition with an unconditional true would therefore still pass this test, although a real browser could immediately capture about:blank. The fabricated screenshot also appends PAGE based on that same flag rather than rendering the HTML, so neither width proves that the saved picture shows the target page.
